national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), principally through its Sede Electrónica. Regional tax authorities administer certain taxes in the Basque Country and Navarre; the target jurisdiction is otherwise Spain's common tax territory.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must obtain a provisional NIF and then a definitive NIF from the AEAT, ordinarily by filing Modelo 036 and providing the deed of incorporation, Mercantile Registry evidence when available, and identification and authority documents for its representatives. The company must register its business activities and tax census details before commencing taxable activities. A foreign entity requiring a Spanish NIF or VAT registration generally files Modelo 036 with evidence of its foreign legal existence, tax residence, representatives, and Spanish taxable activities. A non-EU-established taxable person generally must appoint a Spanish tax representative, subject to applicable statutory exceptions. An EU-established taxable person is generally not required to appoint one. VAT registration is made through the AEAT census process; an EU-established business may instead be required to use the VAT One Stop Shop for eligible cross-border consumer supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no general US-style check-the-box election. An SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate taxable entity. Certain qualifying Spanish civil-law entities and other specified arrangements may be taxed under special transparent or attribution regimes, but these are not elections that convert an SL into a pass-through entity. Spain has no general domestic election permitting an SL to opt into a hybrid classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA); Canary Islands, Ceuta, and Melilla are outside the common Spanish VAT territory and apply different indirect-tax regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general domestic turnover threshold: a taxable person carrying out activities requiring Spanish VAT registration must generally register from the relevant commencement or supply date. Separate rules apply to qualifying cross-border consumer sales, including the EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold for specified intra-EU distance sales and electronically supplied services, and to use of the One Stop Shop.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not generally require real-time AEAT clearance of every domestic VAT invoice. The Immediate Supply of Information system (SII) requires qualifying taxpayers, including large businesses, VAT groups, and certain refund-register taxpayers, to submit invoice-record data electronically, generally within statutory short deadlines. The Veri*Factu invoicing-system rules provide for secure, traceable records and, where applicable, submission to the AEAT; implementation dates and obligations depend on the taxpayer and applicable transitional rules. Law 18/2022 provides for mandatory electronic invoicing between businesses, with phased application subject to implementing regulations. Public-sector invoicing requirements apply separately. Businesses must verify current commencement dates and technical specifications; no universal digital-stamping or advance invoice-clearance obligation applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from the Spanish VAT territory to a destination outside the EU may qualify for exemption with deduction under Article 21 of the Spanish VAT Law, provided the statutory exporter, recipient, and proof-of-exit conditions are met. Intra-EU supplies are governed by separate exemption conditions, including valid VAT identification and evidence of transport. Services are not automatically zero-rated because the customer or provider is abroad: place-of-supply rules determine whether Spanish VAT applies, and any exemption or out-of-scope treatment must be supported under the relevant rule. Virtual-event access and electronically supplied services require transaction-specific place-of-supply analysis.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration and evidence of customs exit, such as the export accompanying document and electronic exit confirmation where available
Commercial invoice, sales contract or order, and records identifying the goods, customer, and transaction
Bill of lading, air waybill, or other transport documentation evidencing dispatch to a destination outside the EU
Proof of payment and accounting records; an inward remittance certificate is not generally a statutory Spanish VAT export document

For services, contracts, customer-location and business-status evidence, deliverables or service-performance records, and payment evidence appropriate to the applicable place-of-supply or exemption rule
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain imposes no general statutory deadline requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days. Export exemption claims must be supported by contemporaneous evidence of the supply, transport, customs exit where relevant, and satisfaction of the applicable legal conditions. Unsupported or fraudulent claims may result in denial or recovery of the exemption or input-tax deduction, late-payment interest, and tax penalties under the General Tax Law. Failure to pay tax may attract penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount depending on classification and severity; serious or very serious infringements, false documentation, and fraudulent conduct may trigger higher sanctions or criminal exposure. Assessments are generally subject to the applicable limitation period, ordinarily four years, subject to statutory interruption and other exceptions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem and the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM). Competences relevant to treasury include: supervision of credit institutions and payment/e-money institutions; operation of the Sistema de Entidades de Notificación (SEN) statistical reporting framework for foreign transactions; maintenance of the official register for currency-exchange and virtual-asset custody service providers under Law 10/2010 (as amended); and advisory role to the Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa on foreign-investment declarations and balance-of-payments concepts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain applies full, unrestricted euro convertibility on both the current account (dividend remittances, royalty payments, service fees) and the capital account (equity contributions, shareholder loans, divestment proceeds) pursuant to Articles 63–66 TFEU. There is no prior exchange-control authorization, central-bank permit, or discretionary approval for resident-to-non-resident profit repatriation. The only residual requirement is an ex-post statistical declaration to the Banco de España, routed through the account bank under the SEN system, for any single operation exceeding EUR 50,000 or cumulative monthly flows exceeding EUR 500,000. Profit remittance remains subject to corporate-law solvency and distributable-reserve conditions under Article 303 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital and to the 19% Non-Resident Income Tax withholding (treaty-reduced where applicable), but no FX conversion license or administrative hurdle applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Spain imposes no statutory surrender timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation obligation on export, digital-service, or virtual-concert ticketing proceeds. The SL may retain receipts in EUR or any freely convertible foreign currency in a commercial-bank foreign-currency account for an indefinite period. The sole compliance duty is statistical: receipts that individually exceed EUR 50,000 or accumulate above EUR 500,000 in a calendar month must be captured in the Banco de España SEN foreign-transaction declaration (goods/services concept code), which the sponsoring bank files electronically; no monetization mandate or minimum conversion applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High, conditional on EU/EEA passporting. A fintech EMI is viable as a treasury overlay only if it holds a valid PSD2/E-Money Directive authorization in an EEA home state and has filed its passport notification with the Banco de España (or is itself a Spanish licensed EMI). Under that condition the EMI may provide settlement-capable EUR IBAN accounts, multi-currency virtual accounts, corporate cards, and USDC-to-euro conversion through a MiCA-licensed crypto-asset service provider. Legal constraints: (i) an unlicensed non-EU EMI cannot lawfully hold Spanish corporate funds or receive Spanish payment flows; (ii) the SL's EUR 3,000 statutory capital and tax-registration nexus should remain with a Tier-1 credit institution while the EMI functions as a disbursement and payout layer; (iii) any stablecoin (USDC is an e-money token under MiCA) settlement leg requires a MiCA-authorized issuer/CASP; US-only off-EU EMIs are not permissible for the Spanish leg.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical branch attendance is not a statutory absolute — Law 10/2010 and R.D. 304/2014 permit certified remote/video identification — but Tier-1 Spanish banks in practice require: (a) the appointed statutory administrator (administrador único or solidario) to attend an in-person KYC interview at the Madrid or Barcelona corporate-banking branch, or alternatively to execute a notarially authenticated power of attorney (poder notarial) before a Spanish notary; (b) every director and any non-resident beneficial owner holding more than 25% to provide passport-level identity documentation and undergo an enhanced virtual interview; (c) fully remote opening remains possible through Santander/BBVA digital corporate onboarding where the signing director holds a valid Spanish NIF and where a certified video-identification session is recorded and retained; (d) a Spanish public notary is mandatory when the capital increase requires a public deed for inscription in the Registro Mercantil.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Stablecoin (USDC) payment-rail exposure and the receipt of recurring virtual-concert ticket sale volumes without physical contractual signatures, giving rise to an inherently bank-flagged money-laundering vector.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written AML/CFT policy of the SL with designated 'representante ante el SEPBLAC'; Stripe merchant-processing agreement proving platform-side KYC/KYB; engagement contract with a MiCA-licensed CASP for the USDC-fiat ramp; independent cybersecurity and wallet-control audit opinion; documented ticket-purchaser sanctions/PEP/velocity screening procedures; GDPR-compliant customer audit trail; auditor's AML attestation confirming transaction monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership without an established Spanish banking or commercial footprint, triggering enhanced due diligence under Article 14 Law 10/2010.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Nota simple from the Registro Mercantil; deed of incorporation and bylaws; completed UBO declaration; certificate of registration in the Registro de Titularidades Reales; apostilled passports and address verification for each natural-person owner above 25%; FATCA/CRS self-certifications; bank reference letter from the foreign relationship bank; shareholder agreement and group organization chart evidencing economic substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border disbursement pattern to LatAm production contractors and metaverse-platform licensing counterparties in jurisdictions with heightened corruption and sanctions ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed vendor contracts with UBO declarations; Spanish VAT-compliant commercial invoice book; transfer-pricing documentation with arm's-length benchmark; quarterly AML risk-scoring memo rating geographic, product, and distribution-channel risk; sanctions-screening evidence with no-match confirmation; auditor-attested reconciliation of every outbound wire to invoice and treasury ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lump-sum inbound capital injection from non-resident shareholders raising concerns about source of funds or indirect nominee structuring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved three-year treasury and ticket-revenue projection; source-of-funds letters corroborated by six months of shareholder bank statements; notarially executed capital-increase deed inscribed in the Registro Mercantil; updated libro registro de socios; declaration to the Spanish Foreign Investment Registry where the non-EU investor subscribes above 10% of share capital or the transaction exceeds EUR 1,000,000; allocation memo showing deployment into latency infrastructure and ticketing technology.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident equity contributions are wired via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer where the shareholder is EU-resident) to the SL's segregated capital escrow account at the Tier-1 bank. The bank tags the receipt under the Banco de España SEN concept family J41 (capital contribution by non-resident) for statistical declaration purposes. Prior to full credit availability, the treasury must deliver: (i) the board resolution approving the injection; (ii) the notarially attested deed of capital increase for inscription in the Registro Mercantil where the injection exceeds EUR 3,000; (iii) the updated shareholder register; (iv) source-of-funds evidence and the UBO declaration; and (v) where the non-EU investor acquires 10% or more of the share capital or the operation exceeds EUR 1,000,000, the ex-post foreign-investment declaration to the Spanish Foreign Investment Registry. The cleared funds become available for platform capex only after the compliance officer releases them from the escrow sub-account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EEA supplier and licensor payments settle via SEPA Credit Transfer / SEPA Instant (SCT Inst) using ISO 20022 pain.001 messages with structured remittance data and IBAN name-check. Non-EEA disbursements execute over SWIFT MT103 with UETR/GPi tracking. For material LatAm production suppliers and metaverse-platform licensing contracts, treasury may issue irrevocable sight documentary letters of credit under ICC UCP600, transmitted via MT700/MT760, or effect prepayment against performance security. Every outbound transfer references the underlying invoice, is tagged with the applicable SEN statistical concept, and flows into the treasury reconciliation system to synchronize Banco de España declarations, CRS, and VAT reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/MXN, EUR/CLP) up to 12-month tenors, documented under ISDA 2002 FX Definitions and booked through the Tier-1 bank treasury; physically settled forwards are outside the EMIR mandatory clearing obligation for non-financial counterparties.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referenced to limited-convertibility LatAm currencies (USD/ARS, USD/VES, USD/BOB) for managing ticket-revenue volatility where no deliverable market exists.
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/MXN, EUR/BRL) for term-matched alignment of deployed paid-in capital with platform-licensing liabilities.
European-style FX options (EUR/USD, EUR/MXN) purchased on a standalone or collar/strangle basis for one-way protection on USD-denominated virtual-ticket conversion.
FX swaps (spot-forward pairings) for intraday EUR/USD liquidity rotation between the operational account and the capital escrow facility without creating interest-rate derivatives exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and corporate UBO declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approve within six months after financial year-end and file within one month after approval; for a 31 December year-end, normally approve by 30 June and file by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure after one year from the financial year-end filing deadline; fines generally range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, with higher limits for larger companies or longer delays. Spain has no automatic administrative strike-off solely for late annual accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year; for a 31 December year-end, normally 1 to 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment generally triggers a surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay, or 15% after more than 12 months, plus statutory interest. Failure to file may also generate tax penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT summary return, Form 390, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally filed during the first 30 calendar days of the following year; certain taxpayers filing periodic VAT returns are exempt.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or incorrect filing may result in fixed tax penalties, generally subject to statutory reductions for voluntary correction and prompt payment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Activities Tax declaration or payment, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria or the competent municipal authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Applicable only where the company is not exempt; payment and declaration dates depend on the taxpayer category and competent authority.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment may trigger surcharges, interest, collection costs, and enforcement proceedings. Most newly formed entities and entities with annual turnover below the statutory threshold are exempt.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is generally mandatory when a company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets exceeding EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover exceeding EUR 5.7 million, or average employees exceeding 50. Audit may also be mandatory for regulated activities, public-interest entities, securities offerings, or other statutory situations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) and applicable Spanish accounting regulations. IFRS is generally mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed groups and may apply in other regulated circumstances.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain accurate beneficial ownership information and update it when ownership or control changes. The annual accounts filing normally includes a beneficial ownership declaration; where no information has changed, the company confirms that the previously filed information remains current. Transfers of shares in an SL must be documented and recorded in the Register of Members; the UBO analysis must be refreshed after each relevant transfer or control change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Contracts with the Sole Shareholder, if applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,600-5,500 for a small Spanish SL, depending on turnover, transaction volume, consolidation, and audit complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 25% standard rate; R&D tax credit (25% of qualifying expenses up to cap); accelerated depreciation; no sector-specific holidays for virtual performance services

tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 25th day of the 4th month following the end of the tax period (e.g. 25 April for calendar year-end 31 December)

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% on dividends to non-residents (reduced to 0-15% under applicable DTAs)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TRC (Treaty Relief Certificate) application to AEAT with ownership proof, beneficial ownership declaration and supporting documentation; obtain prior approval before remitting funds
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 19% statutory (0-10% under DTAs); Interest: 19% statutory (frequently 0% under DTAs for arm's-length debt)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 threshold triggering mandatory Local File documentation for related-party transactions
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain applies OECD/EU economic substance rules; holding, IP and finance entities must demonstrate adequate employees, premises and core income-generating activities in Spain; virtual concert operations require local substance for tax recognition

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil; directors personally liable for unpaid taxes and criminal sanctions for fraudulent setup

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal joint and several liability for the tax debt; imprisonment for willful non-compliance
